Patient ID: 900631438

I would like to share my recent and disappointing experience at Aster Hospital’s Emergency Department in the Mankhool branch.

We arrived at the emergency reception around 5:30 PM, and although it was clearly an emergency (I was in severe abdominal pain), we were only attended to around 5:50 PM—a 20-minute wait despite being in obvious distress. This delay was unacceptable in an emergency setting, especially when patients are supposed to receive immediate attention.

Once I was finally placed on a bed, the doctor examined me, administered a pain reliever, and recommended further tests, including a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis, an IV drip, and blood tests. Despite these steps, I felt neglected throughout the evening. I vomited severely at 11:45 PM and requested to be admitted to a room to rest more comfortably, but that also took a long time. It wasn’t until around 4:00 AM that the CT scan was done, after which I begged again for a room, and was finally moved to Room 406—only after vomiting again.

I must commend one compassionate nurse in the room who truly showed care, his name, Allwin Jeffry - unlike the staff in the emergency room, who lacked empathy and made me feel like a burden instead of a patient in need.

Later in the morning, I requested to be discharged so I could travel to Jordan for treatment with my longtime doctor. I asked for my medical release at 8:30 AM, but even this simple request took an unreasonable amount of time. Although we settled the AED 200 excess payment quickly, the staff delayed my discharge by claiming the printer wasn’t working and insisted I stay in the room—despite everything being settled and my ID already returned.

One male staff member in pink uniform even acted rudely, which made the situation worse. I told him that I was not a prisoner to be held unnecessarily. My driver had to rush through the stairs with proof of payment to ensure I wouldn’t miss my 2 PM flight to Jordan all because of the inefficient discharge process. please review your camera, and he must be given extra seminar on how to handle customer care! this is must for him!

This experience was not only physically painful but also emotionally exhausting!!! I am deeply disappointed by the lack of urgency, care, and compassion shown in the emergency department. Aster Hospital is a large and reputable name, yet this experience was far from what a patient should expect in an emergency medical facility!

I sincerely hope the hospital takes this feedback seriously and works to improve its emergency protocols, discharge procedures, and staff attitude toward patients in pain. No one should have to suffer in such a way while seeking help in a hospital.

Unfortunately, I will not return to this hospital again. Please, train your staff to treat every patient with respect, care, and urgency especially those in critical conditions.

I’ve always had pleasant experiences at Aster Hospital, Mankhool in the past, but my recent visit left me somewhat disappointed.

On 04/10/2025, I requested a replacement vaccination card for my daughter after misplacing the original. I paid the required fees, and the Pediatric Department informed me that I would receive a call once the document was ready. However, I did not receive any follow-up.

By 08/10/2025, still having heard nothing, I contacted the call center, where I was assured the relevant department had been informed and that I would receive a call soon. After another two days without any response, I called again and received the same message.

Due to the lack of communication, I visited the hospital in person on 11/10/2025, expecting the card to be ready given the time that had passed. To my surprise, the request was still pending. I was told that the doctors had not had time to complete the required information, which was frustrating.

After I escalated the matter, the Patient Coordinators stepped in and addressed the issue. I was told the vaccination card would be ready in three days. On 16/10/2025, I finally received a call confirming it was ready for collection.

While I appreciate the support provided by the patient coordination team once the matter was raised, I would like to highlight the need for improvement in the call center's communication and follow-up process.

NB: This review is based on my personal experience—others may have a smoother and more positive experience.

Complaint Regarding Decline in Service Quality at Mediclinic City Hospital

I have been a loyal patient at Mediclinic for over four years. In the past, my experience was excellent, and I trusted your services fully. Unfortunately, over the last two years, the quality of care at City Hospital has declined significantly. I am compelled to raise the following concerns:

1. Misdiagnosis and Negligence (Husband’s Case)
Two years ago, my husband visited the hospital due to bleeding. After a check-up, the doctor concluded that “all is fine.” Recently, we discovered he has gallbladder stones, which by now have grown so large they cannot be dissolved. This represents a clear case of medical negligence. Despite submitting a formal complaint, the representative who contacted us excused and defended the doctor instead of acknowledging responsibility. Until today, no corrective action has been taken.

2. Emergency Visit – Broken Sample and Lack of Communication
I visited the emergency department with severe pain, fever, and diarrhea. I was discharged and asked to leave stool samples for testing. After 15 days, during another appointment, I was informed that the test results never came out because the sample containers were broken. No one contacted me to inform me of this failure, leaving my condition untreated and unresolved.

3. Influenza Diagnosis – Missing Critical Prescription
Two days ago, I was admitted again with 40.2°C fever, chest pain, cough, headache, and body pain. I was diagnosed with influenza, and the doctor clearly stated Tamiflu would be prescribed. However, upon reviewing my medications later, I realized Tamiflu was never given — despite being the primary treatment for influenza. This is a serious error that put my health at risk.

4. Pediatrician department
We came running with our baby with high fever to see if we can get a walking appointment, Pediatrician replied to us: "go to emergency because I am in a photo shooting right now" in this a proper and professional answer?

5. General Decline in Patient Care
While there are a few excellent doctors who truly care for their patients, many others appear to treat patients as tasks, without empathy or proper attention. Often, patients feel rushed or dismissed instead of being properly heard. This mechanical, “robotic” approach is very concerning, because we aren't taking this health service for free,  through our insurance a lot of money has been paid.

6. Cultural Representation of Staff
Given Dubai’s multicultural environment, I strongly recommend Mediclinic consider hiring more doctors and nurses from diverse nationalities. Patients often feel more comfortable expressing sensitive issues in a culturally familiar environment, which would improve trust and satisfaction.

These repeated incidents reflect a pattern of negligence, poor communication, and lack of accountability. Mediclinic was once a trusted name for my family, but my recent experiences at City Hospital have left us deeply disappointed and concerned for our safety as patients.

I urge you to take immediate corrective action, investigate these cases properly, and ensure higher standards of patient care are restored. Otherwise, you risk losing the trust of long-standing patients like myself.
